html:
The movement of Slavic peoples south across the Danube into the Balkans in the 500s and 600s. It is the origin of the South Slavic nations: Serbs, Croats, Bulgarians, Slovenes, Bosniaks, Montenegrins and Macedonians.

Slavic bands first raided Roman lands across the Danube in the reign of Justinian I. From the 570s, often with the Avars, who had settled in Pannonia, they began to settle for good, while the Eastern Roman Empire was busy with wars against Persia. By the 600s they had spread over most of the peninsula, deep into Greece, and Roman towns shrank to walled ports on the coast.

In 681 the Turkic Bulgars founded a state south of the Danube and merged with the Slavs there. Byzantium slowly won back Greece and converted the Slavs. In the 800s the mission of Cyril and Methodius gave them written Slavonic, and later the Cyrillic script.
sum: The movement of Slavic peoples south across the Danube into the Balkans in the 500s and 600s. It is the origin of the South Slavic nations: Serbs, Croats, Bulgarians, Slovenes, Bosniaks, Montenegrins and Macedonians.
